headline: Super Facialist's best-sellers already have strong listings. The upside is in where the ad budget goes, and in a Rosehip range that's set up in a way that holds its cleansing balm back.

points.title: Rosehip Cleansing Balm: move it out of Day Care and give it its own variation family
points.detail: The balm (part of a ~£17k/mo family) is listed under Moisturisers › Day Care and shares one variation family with a day cream, night cream and facial oil, so it competes against moisturisers rather than other cleansing balms. Moving it to Cleansing Balms and splitting the family by product type is the single biggest fix for the product the Brand Store leads with.
evidence: B0D6BWBYY2 category leaf: Day Care (Keepa)
Parent B0F8R55N8X live children: Cleansing Balm, SPF15 Day Cream, Overnight Night Cream, Rose Miracle Facial Oil
Family revenue ~£17,394/mo; balm 882 units/mo at £14 (Jungle Scout)
11 sellers on the balm listing; Amazon holds the Buy Box

points.title: Stop paying for 'super' and unrelated searches across all best-sellers
points.detail: Every best-seller has a sponsored ranking on 'super' (12.5k searches/mo, sponsored #1 for the Cleansing Oil), and each one also shows ads on terms with nothing to do with it, from 'claudia winkleman' and 'no 7 foundation' on the balm to 'claritin' on the blemish wash. That looks like auto or broad campaigns drifting. Negatives plus a search-term review would free budget for the terms below.
evidence: 'super' (12,490/mo): sponsored #1 Cleansing Oil, #2 Salicylic Wash, #4 Micro Polish, #10 Cleansing Balm
Cleansing Balm sponsored on: st eval, bare anatomy rosemary and rice water spray, claudia winkleman, no 7 foundation, witch hazel liquid
Cleansing Oil sponsored on: bioderma micellar water, garnier micellar water, isoclean, nothora
Salicylic Face Wash sponsored on: sudosalve, claritin, mario badescu
Source: Jungle Scout keywords by ASIN, sponsored rank with no organic rank

points.title: Vitamin C Cleansing Oil: take the hero into generic cleanser searches
points.detail: The Cleansing Oil is the engine (~£39.7k/mo, 5,300 reviews, 4.5★) and already ranks on page 2–3 for big generic terms with no ad support: 'face cleanser' (22k/mo, organic #36) and 'facial cleanser' (8k/mo, #30). Exact-match Sponsored Products at the top of search on those terms is the quickest way to grow its best product.
evidence: B00KZYWQLM: 5,315 units/mo, £7.47 (Jungle Scout), 4.5★ from 5,303 reviews
face cleanser: 22,136/mo, organic #36, no sponsored rank, CPC ~£0.96
facial cleanser: 7,989/mo, organic #30, no sponsored rank, CPC ~£0.75
Selling at £7.47 against a £12 list price (38% off), so check the discount is funded

points.title: Salicylic Blemish Face Wash: advertise on 'face wash' and acne terms
points.detail: This ~£12.9k/mo family has 2,000+ reviews but is sponsored on only 15 terms, some of them unrelated. It ranks organically for 'face wash' (82k/mo, #45), 'salicylic acid' (36k/mo, #48) and 'acne face wash' (#25) with no ads, at low CPCs (~£0.24–0.54).
evidence: B07K1Z7Q7V: 1,592 units/mo at £6.30, 4.4★ from 2,065 reviews
face wash: 82,259/mo, organic #45, CPC ~£0.39
salicylic acid: 36,360/mo, organic #48, CPC ~£0.24
acne face wash: 4,093/mo, organic #25, CPC ~£0.54

points.title: Quick wins: tidy two more mixed families and the night cream's resellers
points.detail: The Salicylic wash shares a family with a toner, and the Vegan Collagen Night Cream shares one with a cleanser, moisturiser and serum. The night cream has 17 sellers and is selling at £20 against a £12.50 list price, which points to reseller pricing to rein in through Brand Registry.
evidence: Parent B0H2BDYNF4: face wash + toner
Parent B0D9LRH3ZN: night cream + cleanser + moisturiser + serum
B0CSPJHQRC: 17 sellers, £20.00 vs £12.50 list (Keepa)
B00IEU6OF8 titled 'Superfacialist…' rather than 'Super Facialist'

hero_actions.B00KZYWQLM: Exact-match SP on 'face cleanser' and 'facial cleanser'; negative 'super' and the micellar-water terms.
hero_actions.B0D6BWBYY2: Move to Cleansing Balms and split it out of the Rosehip 'Style' family, then cut the unrelated sponsored terms.
hero_actions.B014MI41AU: Test SP on 'face wash women' (organic #27) and 'face exfoliator' (#26); check the 50% discount is deliberate.
hero_actions.B07K1Z7Q7V: Advertise on 'face wash', 'salicylic acid' and 'acne face wash'; separate it from the toner.
hero_actions.B0CSPJHQRC: Bring reseller pricing back to list via Brand Registry, then split the family by product type.

content_note: Content isn't the problem: every best-seller has 7–9 images, video and A+. The Vegan Collagen Night Cream has the thinnest bullets and only 50 reviews.
ad_strategy_summary: Fund the generic cleanser and face-wash terms where the best-sellers already rank on page 2–3, paid for by cutting 'super' and the unrelated terms. An indicative £1.2k–1.9k a month covers the focus terms below.
amc_hypotheses: Every live product offers Subscribe & Save in a consumable category, so repeat buyers are probably a large share of Cleansing Oil revenue.
Searches for 'super facialist cleansing oil' show more than ten competitor ads, so some shoppers looking for the brand are likely buying a rival's cleanser instead.
amc_questions: How many Cleansing Oil buyers come back, and after how many days?
What share of ad-driven sales are new-to-brand on generic cleanser terms versus brand terms?
Which product do new customers buy first, and what do they buy next?
How many shoppers who search the brand name end up buying another brand?
